name: PulseIQ heart-disease screening model

dataset_source.name: UCI Heart Disease (Cleveland processed)
dataset_source.citation: Janosi, A., Steinbrunn, W., Pfisterer, M., Detrano, R. (1988). Heart Disease. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C52P4X
transformations: dropped 6 records with a missing value (ca x4, thal x2) instead of imputing them
renamed the 13 predictor columns to the names the model uses
binarised num (0-4 angiographic severity): target = 1 if num > 0 else 0
exact duplicate feature vectors: none in this export

split: Exact duplicate rows removed before splitting (drop_duplicates), then a single stratified 80/20 train/test split (random_state=42) on the distinct feature vectors. Metrics are on that held-out split; a 10-fold stratified CV is reported alongside for stability. Duplicates are never shared between train and test.
target_encoding: 1 = disease, 0 = no disease (num > 0), verified from feature means
metrics_note: Metrics come from distinct rows only. Earlier revisions trained on a Kaggle copy that had 723 duplicate rows in 1,025 and an inverted target, and reported ROC-AUC and recall of 1.000; that figure is withdrawn, not reproduced here. This run uses the UCI Cleveland original (CC BY 4.0) with 6 incomplete records dropped. Calibration (Brier, ECE) is measured on out-of-fold predictions, one per distinct patient.
